_comment: Every product that has appeared in any Breakpoint MCP competitive-analysis sweep,
carried forward permanently.  An entry is never dropped: products that stop moving
are marked `dormant` or `archive` and keep their ruling, so a later sweep does not
re-litigate a question already answered.
`assetlib_version` / `assetlib_modify_date` are what the live Asset Library API
served when this entry was last reconciled; scripts/assetlib_sweep.py compares
the live API against them and reports anything that moved.
`last_analysed` is the date of the last SOURCE-LEVEL pass, which is a stronger
claim than a version check.  When a sweep reports an entry moved, it owes a
source-level pass; when it reports no change, `no change since <last_analysed>`
is a complete and sufficient result for that entry.
House terminology: these are ALTERNATIVE MCP SERVERS, not rivals.  See
docs/LANDSCAPE_TRACKING_POLICY.md.
🆕 291 — THIS ROSTER HAS TWO POPULATIONS, AND THE SPLIT IS THE POINT.
`entries` are products READ AT SOURCE, each with a ruling: debugger, real_dap_client,
real_lsp_client, csharp, protocol_revision and a note. The cost of a row here is a
source-level pass, so a row is ELECTED and never automatic.
`surfaced` are products a DISCOVERY LEG has seen, carried permanently, holding only
what the leg itself supplies: channel, repository slug, package, version, publish date
and the session that first saw them. No capability claim, because no one has read them.
The cost of a row here is one row, so EVERY project any leg surfaces owes one, and
`assetlib_sweep.py --check` refuses when one is missing.
🔴 WHY IT IS TWO AND NOT ONE. Until 291 the sweep had a single severity — a
never-tracked MCP-shaped entry owed a source-level pass — which was affordable while
the population was ONE channel serving roughly ten new entries a year. The first run
across three channels surfaced fifty. A rule demanding fifty source-level passes in one
commit does not produce fifty analyses; it produces a gate that is red forever and a
roster nobody can make green. Fifty rows with the capability fields blank would be
worse still: that is a coverage claim nobody made.
`channel` records where a product SHIPS, and it is optional. Forty-five entries predate
the channel legs and nobody has recorded where any of them ships; `assetlib_sweep.py
--census` prints that count as `unclassified` rather than defaulting it, so the number
is a visible intake that falls as sessions classify rows.

entries.name: beckett-godot-mcp
entries.note: SOURCE PASS 306 — 947ee6b -> 57f3422 is ONE commit, v1.14.0 -> v1.15.0, 10 files, +333/-15, and the whole window is export hygiene. New core/export_filter.gd is an EditorExportPlugin that skip()s everything under res://addons/beckett/ except one stub, behind project setting beckett/strip_from_exports (default true); its own header (export_filter.gd:8-16) gives the reason — the plugin's autoload was baked into every export preset and Godot's default filter sweeps addons/, so ~480 KB of editor-only GDScript shipped into each game. New runtime/beckett_autoload.gd replaces the old direct autoload target: it names only Node/OS/String at parse time and load()s the real runtime behind OS.has_feature("editor") (:35-38), with duplicate-autoload tie-break for projects upgrading from the godot_mcp rename (:39-49, :70-77). plugin.gd (+64/-2) gained _install_runtime_autoload() re-pointing a pre-existing autoload and persisting via ProjectSettings.save() (:126-146) and _autoload_target() normalising both the legacy *res:// singleton-marker form and Godot 4.4+ *uid:// (:150-160). A new test group _t_export_safety() (tests/unit_tests.gd, +109) asserts the stub names only Node/OS/ResourceLoader-class identifiers, contains no preload(, carries the literal OS.has_feature("editor") gate, and that plugin.gd's RUNTIME_SCRIPT and export_filter.gd's KEEP name the same path, so the two halves cannot drift apart. 🟢 55 TOOLS, UNCHANGED, BY TWO AGREEING DERIVATIONS AT 57f3422: 55 registry.register({ name literals across addons/beckett/tools/*.gd and 55 entries in the generated glama/tools.json, identical sets; tests/ci-smoke.ps1 -ExpectedTools 55 (ci.yml:288) asserts the same and already did at 947ee6b. Zero tool names added or removed — no file under tools/ moved in this window at all. Capabilities re-verified rather than carried: no DAP and no LSP, zero hits for either repo-wide, and zero for breakpoint, step_over and stack_frame (the three 'scopes' hits are plain English). csharp stays TRUE on the same evidence — tools/csharp_tools.gd:29 registers build_csharp and :62 shells out to dotnet build — and that file is untouched here. core/effort.gd is byte-identical between the two commits: 91 tool names across six cumulative tiers (16/25/5/11/26/8), of which the L1-L4 union is 57 and 55 register in this MIT Lite edition; panel.gd:1640-1642 states that Lite trims modules whose tools are still named in _DELTA (list_skills and load_skill live in the Full-only skill_tools) and filters against registry.has() before display, so the 91/55 split predates this window rather than being part of it. The only README prose change is number catch-up — Lite '50 tools' -> '55 tools', Full '80 tools, 37 skill packs' -> '91 tools, 46 skill packs' — and both figures were already true of the tree at 947ee6b, so the document moved and the surface did not. 🔵 AND THE CARD IS THE HALF THAT HAS NOT MOVED THIS TIME: the Asset Library listing still reads 1.14.0 (2026-08-26) against a source at 1.15.0, which is the exact inverse of the 284 pass, where the source was read first and the card caught up hours later. assetlib_version stays at what the card says, because it is a reading of the card and not of the repository.

entries.note: SOURCE PASS 284. bd1b8e4..b91650c is two commits, 24 files, +842/-39, and it is auth and UX only — no tool and no transport change. A 'D4 assisted ladder' (GodotAssistedSignIn.cs) auto-opens the browser at the device-auth verification URL once per editor session; GodotAccountAuth.cs re-hooks SignInRequired/AuthStateChanged across provider swaps; and a silent-failure fix in ConnectionPanelView.cs, where a dead machine-store credential previously rendered nothing for a signed-in user. 42 tools by two agreeing derivations ([AiTool] attributes; and the first positional argument of every [AiTool(] block with ToolId constants resolved) — of which 39 are advertised to MCP clients, the other three being System tools routed to a disjoint registry reachable only over HTTP /api/system-tools/. DEBUGGER STILL 'none', with a nuance worth recording: there IS structured runtime-error capture via the Godot 4.5+ OS.AddLogger hook plus AppDomain.UnhandledException, surfacing multi-frame ScriptBacktrace data through runtime-errors-get — richer than log scraping, but passive post-hoc diagnostics with no execution control, so not a debugger. No DAP and no LSP: zero repo-wide hits for Content-Length, setBreakpoints, :6005 or textDocument. C# is real and total — the addon IS C# and needs the .NET Godot build — but script-validate is GDScript-only by its own comment, since there is no in-editor C# compiler to reach cheaply. Cloud-first: the addon is a SignalR client dialling a hosted backend at ai-game.dev or a self-hosted URL. Effectively single-maintainer, 220 of 221 commits.

entries.name: godot-agent-loop
entries.note: SOURCE PASS 284 — card said no change, head moved 2c6127b -> 3148cda, and this window is real behaviour: 13 commits, 26 files, +896/-71, with ~490 lines of new tests and no version bump (3.0.0 both ends). 🔴 ROSTER CORRECTION: csharp was recorded false and is TRUE — verify_dotnet_project (inspect|restore|build|run) probes dotnet --version and runs restore/build against a versioned Godot.NET.Sdk. Unchanged in this window, so the roster value was already wrong at the previously recorded commit. The substantive change is child-environment sanitization: every spawned Godot process now gets a 22-key allowlist rather than inheriting process.env, on the stated reasoning that project GDScript runs with the user's OS permissions and can therefore read any inherited credential. Short-lived CLI runs additionally get GODOT_MCP_RUNTIME_DISABLED=true so validate/test/import/export never open a runtime listener. Startup failures now surface instead of hanging — a GameStartupError carrying exitCode/signal, thrown when the process exits during the connect delay. 56 tools by three agreeing routes (rawToolDefinitions; the toolManifest record keys; the handler dispatch keys), unchanged across the window. Only 16 core tools are advertised by default, the other 40 reached through godot_catalog progressive disclosure, against a pinned context budget. No DAP, and LSP is explicitly scoped OUT in docs/coverage/engine-scope.json: diagnostics come from validate_script via --check-only rather than from driving the language server. Node stdio sidecar plus an authenticated loopback TCP channel to an injected in-game interaction server. Card is at 1.0.0 against a source 3.0.0.

entries.assetlib_title: Wick — C# MCP Server for Godot
entries.note: SOURCE PASS 284, and this entry is why Rule 2 has a second clause: the Asset Library card has not moved since 2026-04-26 and the head moved 99806df -> 5540357. Reading it: FIVE commits, all 2026-08-13, 3 files, +10/-10 — Dependabot bumps (MessagePack, Roslyn, Microsoft.Extensions.*) and one CI action. No src/, tests/ or addons/ file touched; the tool surface, DAP, LSP and C# paths are byte-identical. 'Nothing that matters changed' is the finding, and it is a MEASURED one. 64 tools by two agreeing derivations ([McpServerTool] attributes across 12 [McpServerToolType] classes; and the declarative catalog in DefaultToolGroups.cs) — agreement is CI-enforced by DefaultToolGroupsTests.cs, not coincidence. Only 17 are advertised out of the box: tools are gated into five opt-in pillars via WICK_GROUPS, defaulting to core. Still the only tracked entry with BOTH a real DAP client and a real LSP client, and both are confirmed at source: GodotDapClient.cs opens a raw TcpClient to 127.0.0.1:6006 with hand-rolled Content-Length framing and an adapterID=godot initialize handshake; GodotLspClient.cs speaks LSP to 127.0.0.1:6005 and a second CSharpLspClient.cs spawns csharp-ls over stdio. SCOPE CAVEAT WORTH CARRYING: the DAP verbs are launch, configurationDone, stackTrace, evaluate and variables — there is no setBreakpoints and no continue/step, so it is a real DAP client with launch-and-inspect verbs rather than debug-session control. C# is the centre of gravity, not a bolt-on: MSBuildWorkspace, GetSemanticModel, SymbolFinder, with tests. VERSION DIVERGENCE: source has been 1.0.0 since tag v1.0.0 while the card still reads 0.1.0 — one major version and four months behind, which is the sharpest evidence in this roster that an Asset Library version is not a usable freshness signal. Cadence: last substantive source commit 2026-04-30; everything since is Dependabot or CI. Maintained rather than developed. 🆕 294 — `cadence` was the free text 'dependency-only since 2026-04-30' until this session made the column a field a gate reads; it described commit SHAPE rather than release frequency, and nobody has measured a frequency, so it is `unknown` — the STRICT bucket, which buys the shortest staleness window rather than the longest.

entries.name: coding-solo-godot-mcp
entries.note: 🔴 THE ENTRY THIS ROSTER'S POPULATION WAS BLIND TO, AND THE MOST-STARRED PROJECT IN THE CATEGORY. 5,399 stars at the 2026-08-27 reading against hi-godot/godot-ai's 1,954, which this roster and two published analyses both called the clear popularity leader; that claim was wrong for as long as it was made and no health in the Asset Library leg could have said so. Ships on npm only — verified by grepping every .md/.json/.gd/.ts/.yml in the repository for Asset Library install instructions, zero hits. 14 tools, MIT, last commit 2026-04-16. It is the UPSTREAM of tugcantopaloglu/godot-mcp, which this roster has tracked since it had 439 stars. 🟢 Credit where it is due (Rule 4): it has a visible security posture — external hardening pull requests for shell injection and arbitrary GDScript instantiation were merged promptly. `last_analysed_commit` is deliberately null: the 2026-08-27 pass recorded capabilities, not a SHA, and 284's rule is that a baseline nobody read is worse than an honest `unread`.

entries.name: satelliteoflove-godot-mcp
entries.note: 🟢 THE MOST ACTIVE PROJECT IN THE CATEGORY AND THE ONE WITH THE BROADEST CI, AND SAYING SO IS RULE 4 WORKING. 21 tools / 88 actions, MIT, 309 commits with a release cut on the day it was read. MCP revision 2025-06-18, SDK 1.30.0. Roughly 458 TypeScript tests, 24 GDScript headless tests and 8 agent evals across 4 CI workflows, including a wire-level protocol smoke test against the BUILT artifact and tool-schema snapshot tests — a shape worth learning from. Deterministic game-time control: `freeze` / `step` / `step_until` / `thaw`. It is the first project found on all three enumerable channels at once (npm, the official MCP Registry, GitHub Releases), which is what makes it the fold's own positive control.

entries.name: ryanmazzolini-minimal-godot-mcp
entries.note: 🟢 A FOURTH REAL DAP CLIENT, AND IT MOVED NOTHING — WHICH IS RULE 4's DEPTH RULE DEMONSTRATED RATHER THAN ARGUED. It opens a socket to port 6006 and speaks the Debug Adapter Protocol, and to port 6005/6007 for LSP, so `real_dap_client` and `real_lsp_client` are both true. Measured at source: it sends exactly TWO DAP requests — `initialize` and `attach` — and uses the connection as a pipe for `output` events. Its four tools are `get_diagnostics`, `scan_workspace_diagnostics`, `get_console_output`, `clear_console_output`. No breakpoints, no stepping, no stack trace, no scopes, no variables, no C#. So the category now has four projects with a real DAP client and the number that can step through a breakpoint is unchanged: an existence claim would have decayed here for the fourth time; the depth claim did not move at all.

entries.name: hybridindie-godot-mcp
entries.note: 🔴 THE DEEPEST EDITOR-DEBUGGER SURFACE ON THIS ROSTER, AND THE FIRST PASS IS ITS FIRST. Surfaced by the Asset Library leg at 292 as a never-tracked MCP-shaped entry (card 2026-08-27); the repository is three months old, 246 commits from one author, MIT. A Python FastMCP server (fastmcp==4.0.0b3) listening on ws://localhost:9080 (mcp_server/bridge.py:Bridge.serve) paired with a GDScript EditorPlugin that connects as the WebSocket client; mcp_server/tools/*.py delegate through _route.route to cmd_* handlers in godot/addons/godot_mcp/handlers/. 🟢 TOOL COUNT VERIFIED TWO WAYS AND THE CARD IS ACCURATE: 180, by grep over `@mcp.tool(` registrations and independently by enumerating Provider.list_tools(create_server()), across the 29 tags declared in mcp_server/categories.py. 🔴 THE DEBUGGING CATEGORY IS REAL AND IT IS COMPLETE ON THE EDITOR PLANE: godot/addons/godot_mcp/mcp_debugger.gd is an EditorDebuggerPlugin installed with add_debugger_plugin, and its eleven godot_debugger_* tools cover breakpoints (EditorDebuggerSession.set_breakpoint), stepping (send_message with step/next/out plus continue, each guarded by is_breaked()), stack frames (get_stack_dump), frame variables (get_stack_frame_vars, returning locals/members/globals) and expression evaluation (evaluate). Every earlier entry on this roster with the same `debugger` value stops short of one or more of those. 🔵 THE DEPTH CLAIM HAS A CEILING AND IT IS IN THE TRANSPORT: replies arrive asynchronously and are claimed back through _has_capture, so each read tool returns the PREVIOUSLY CACHED payload and then requests a refresh — poll-and-cache, one call behind (mcp_debugger.gd module docstring; _cmd_get_stack_frames). It also requires a live play session, and force_break additionally requires the game to carry the mcp_runtime_probe.gd autoload. No DAP client and no port 6006 anywhere (docs/debugger_feasibility.md:9 records the choice of EditorDebuggerSession.send_message explicitly); no LSP; C# appears only as a ".cs": "CSharpScript" import lookup at mcp_server/tools/import_asset.py:51. Default surface is 18 of 180 — mcp_server/toolsets.py:DEFAULT_ENABLED is inspection plus always-on core, and the debugger toolset must be unlocked with enable_toolset; gating is server-global rather than per-session, justified in-source by the sessionless 2026-07-28 protocol. 611 test functions and four CI workflows gating ruff, mypy strict and a zero-skip scan. 🔵 The card is one release behind the repository (2026.08.26b1 against tag 2026.08.31b3) and the tool count is unchanged across both. 🔴 `last_analysed_commit` is the SHA READ, 037b00f, and not the tag: the first draft of this row recorded `2026.08.31b3` and `source_state` refused it on the spot, because Rule 2's second clause compares a commit and a tag name can never equal one. The tag points one commit earlier at 38196d7; the pass was taken at the branch head. 🟢 RE-READ AT 293, 037b00f -> 2400578, AND THE RULING HOLDS — a source pass and not a baseline bump (292 §6 forbade the latter). Twelve files changed and exactly one of them falls under the recorded `capability_paths`: mcp_server/tools/undo.py, which declares an explicit output_schema on the EXISTING `undo` tool because UndoResult's @model_serializer degenerates FastMCP's auto-derived schema (their issue #385) — no tool added and none removed. The registration count is 180 at BOTH commits by the same derivation; mcp_debugger.gd, toolsets.py and categories.py are byte-identical across the range, and godot/addons/godot_mcp/ moved only plugin.cfg's version string to 2026.08.31b4. The remainder is documentation and two new contract test files (test_output_schema.py, test_sessionless_invariants.py). 🔵 So the move was MATERIAL by the paths and IMMATERIAL in fact, which is the reader working: it turned `the head moved, pay a pass' into `read one file'.

entries.name: godot-mcp-runtime
entries.note: 🟢 THE TOP-RANKED PROJECT ON THE SURFACED LIST AND THE FIRST ONE THE RANKING ELECTED. Surfaced by the npm and MCP-registry legs at 291 and unread for twenty-three sessions; at 314 it reads 66 stars and 3,000 npm downloads in thirty days, which is the highest download count of any surfaced row and the second-highest star count. TypeScript, MIT, 36 tools in `allToolDefinitions` (src/index.ts:29) across six files, registered through the SDK's raw `ListToolsRequestSchema` handler rather than `registerTool`. It drives the engine two ways: headless `--headless --script` runs of a generated GDScript operation file (src/utils/godot-runner.ts, src/scripts/godot_operations.gd, 43 KB), and a live TCP bridge to a running game (src/scripts/mcp_bridge.gd, src/utils/bridge-protocol.ts) on 127.0.0.1 — the 'runtime' the name refers to. 🔴 IT DOCUMENTS ITS OWN ABSENCE OF A DEBUGGER, WHICH IS THE STRONGEST SOURCE A `false` CAN HAVE: src/index.ts:55 — *run_project spawns Godot without -d so runtime errors do not pause execution; the `breakpoint` keyword in user code is a no-op (no debugger is attached)*. No DAP, no LSP and no C# string anywhere under src/ or the shipped GDScript. 🔵 Its MCP revision is a real reading rather than an SDK default: src/utils/structured-response.ts:8 and docs/tool-authoring.md:61 both cite revision 2025-06-18 for the `structuredContent` requirement, and the project routes every success path through a helper that satisfies it — which is a client-compatibility concern Breakpoint answers the same way. SDK ^1.25.2.

entries.name: better-godot-mcp
entries.note: 🔵 THE ONE PROJECT ON THIS ROSTER WHOSE DESIGN CLAIM IS ABOUT TOOL COUNT GOING DOWN. 37 stars and 2,141 npm downloads in thirty days at 314; TypeScript, Apache-2.0, and SEVENTEEN tools, each a composite verb with an `action` parameter rather than one tool per operation — project, scenes, nodes, scripts, editor, config, help, resources, input_map, signals, animation, tilemap, shader, physics, audio, navigation, ui (src/tools/registry.ts, seventeen top-level `name:` keys). That is the opposite bet from `yanhuifair/Godot-MCP`'s 386 and worth watching as a position rather than as a capability: a small surface is a claim about client context budgets, which is the same argument `token-cost.mjs` measures on this side. It ships an EditorPlugin addon (addons/better_godot_mcp/, a 10 KB dock) beside a headless detector (src/godot/detector.ts, src/godot/headless.ts). 🔴 NO DEBUGGER, NO DAP, NO LSP AND NO C#: none of those strings appear anywhere under src/ or addons/ at dd88f0e. 🔵 Its revision reading is explicit and NEWER than most of this roster — src/tools/registry.ts:545 writes *Envelope-loose output schema (spec 2025-11-25)* — and src/init-server.ts:75 cites a 2026-05-01 stdio/http multiuser spec document by filename, so it is tracking the protocol actively. SDK ^1.30.0.

entries.name: yanhuifair-godot-mcp
entries.note: 🔴 THE LARGEST TOOL SURFACE ON THIS ROSTER, AND IT IS LARGER THAN ITS OWN PACKAGE SAYS. 386 registrations in src/tools/register.ts (`.register(` calls, one file, 94 KB) against the 358 its npm description advertises — the published claim is 28 behind the tree at cd5da3c. 23 stars and 2,528 npm downloads in thirty days; TypeScript, AGPL-3.0-or-later, which is the only copyleft licence on this roster and a real consideration for anyone embedding it. It pairs a 90 KB EditorPlugin (addons/godot-mcp/plugin.gd) with a TCP editor bridge on 127.0.0.1:9876 (addons/godot-mcp/runtime_bridge.gd, src/tools/runtime_bridge.ts) and a set of pure parsers for .tscn, .tres and project.godot (src/parsers/) that read the files without the engine. 🔵 ITS DEBUGGER IS THE ENGINE'S OWN AND NOTHING MORE: src/tools/godot.ts:39 exposes a `Run with debugger` boolean that adds `-d` to the launch, and src/tools/meta.ts:108 describes the bridge as *editor bridge (live scene/node/script/debugger control on :9876)* — the editor's debugger panel driven over a private socket, which is the `godot-internal-editor-debugger` ruling this roster already has a name for. No DAP client, no LSP client. 🔴 AND ITS C# IS A FILE EXTENSION, NOT A TOOLCHAIN: the only `.cs` in the tree is src/tools/project.ts:676, where it is one member of a list of extensions a file walk collects — no dotnet invocation, no csproj, no build. 🔵 `protocol_revision` is deliberately absent: the server pins no revision string anywhere and inherits whatever SDK ^1.29.0 negotiates, so recording a date here would be a reading of the dependency rather than of this project.
